test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: On 8th March 2025, the nation observed the Jayanti of which social reformer and founder of the Matua Sect, known for leading the Chandal movement against untouchability?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shree Harichand Thakur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shree Harichand Thakur** was a prominent **social reformer and spiritual leader** who founded the **Matua Sect**, a religious and social movement aimed at uplifting the downtrodden and marginalized communities.
 
• He is known for initiating and leading the **Chandal movement**, which was directed against the practice of **untouchability** and social discrimination faced by the oppressed communities, particularly the Chandals (a Dalit community).
 
• Shree Harichand Thakur emphasized the principles of **equality, social justice, and humanity**. His teachings were focused on eradicating caste-based discrimination and promoting dignity for all human beings.
 
• His followers, known as **Matuas**, played a significant role in spreading his message across Bengal and other parts of India. The Matua Sect continues to be a major spiritual and social movement, especially among the Dalit communities.
 
• The **8th of March 2025** marked the observance of his **Jayanti** (birth anniversary), showcasing his contribution to the fight against social inequality and untouchability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Matua Sect:**

 
 
• The Matua Sect was founded by **Shree Harichand Thakur** in the **19th century** in Bengal.
 
• It is a socio-religious reform movement aimed at uplifting the **economically and socially weaker sections**, particularly the Dalits and marginalized communities.
 
• The movement emphasizes **spirituality, equality, and social reform**, rejecting caste-based discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Chandal Movement:**
 
 
• It was a significant social reform movement led by Shree Harichand Thakur against the practice of **untouchability**.
 
• The movement aimed to abolish the stigmatization of the Chandal community and ensure their **social dignity and rights**.
 
• The Chandal movement is considered a key milestone in the history of India's social reform movements.
 
 
 
• **Teachings of Shree Harichand Thakur:**
 
 
• He emphasized the principles of **truthfulness, simplicity, and equality**.
 
• His teachings encouraged people to reject caste-based discrimination and practice **universal brotherhood**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Shree Harichand Thakur's efforts led to significant social changes in Bengal and laid the foundation for **Dalit empowerment**.
 
• His followers continue to celebrate his teachings and principles through various cultural and religious practices.
 
• In modern times, the Matua Sect has also gained political significance in regions with a significant Dalit population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shree Narayan Guru:** A social reformer from Kerala, known for his work in promoting equality and abolishing caste-based discrimination in the region. He was not associated with the Matua Sect.
 
• **Shree Jyotirao Phule:** A social reformer from Maharashtra, known for his efforts in women's education and the upliftment of oppressed communities. He was not connected to the Matua Sect.
 
• **Shree Guru Ravidas:** A Bhakti movement saint and poet from North India, known for his spiritual teachings advocating equality and social justice. He was not associated with the Chandal movement or the Matua Sect.
